div.head: I Cn 25
div.ab: ⁊ we lærað eac georne manna gehwylcne, þæt he Godes ege hæbbe symle on his gemynde, ⁊ dæges ⁊ nihtes forhtige for synnum, Domdæg ondræde ⁊ for helle agríse, ⁊ æfre him gehende endedæges wene.
And we lærað eac georne manna gehwylcne, þæt he Godes ege hæbbe symle on his geminde, ⁊ dæges ⁊ nihtes forhtige for sinnum, Dómdæg ondræde ⁊ for helle agrise, ⁊ æfre him gehende endes dæges wene.
⁊ we lærað eac georne manna gehwylcne, þæt he Godes ege hæbbe symble on his gemynde, ⁊ dæges ⁊ nihtes for[h]tige for synnum, Domesdæg ondræde ⁊ for helle agríse, ⁊ æfre him gehende endedæges wene.
Et omnes Dei timorem et amorem in mente habeant, diebus ac noctibus a peccatis fugiant, diem iudicii metuant et inferni cruciatus, et semper ultimum uitę suę terminum cogitent aduenisse.
⁊ we lærað eac georne manna gehwylcne, þæt he Godes ege hæbbe symble on his gemynde, ⁊ dæges ⁊ nihtes forhtige for synnum, Domesdæg ondrǽde ⁊ for helle agrise, ⁊ æfre him gehénde endedæges wene.

And likewise we earnestly enjoin all men to have the fear of God constantly in their hearts, and day and night to be in terror of sin, dreading the Day of Judgment and shuddering at the thought of hell, and ever expecting their last day to be close at hand.

Und wir ermahnen auch ernstlich jeden Menschen, dass er Gottesfurcht immer in seinem Gedächtniss habe und bei Tage und Nachts sich vor Sünden fürchte, vor dem [jüngsten] Gerichtstage bange und vor der Hölle schaudere und stets den letzten [Lebens]tag sich nahe vorstelle.

And we also earnestly instruct everyone to have the fear of God always in mind, and by day and night to be afraid of sins, to dread Judgment Day and shudder at hell, and always to expect his last day to be near.
div.note: Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G
